chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not give anyone less than a head.

key_terms.رَأْسٍ: head (a unit of measure or currency, often referring to a specific coin or weight)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of charity one should give to a poor person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defining the minimum valid amount of charity as 'a head' (*ra's*), a unit of measurement often interpreted as a handful or a specific weight of food. This establishes a legal floor to prevent the devaluation of charity through trivial amounts, ensuring the recipient receives a dignified and meaningful portion rather than mere crumbs. The emphasis on 'meaningful portion' reflects the Shia jurisprudential focus on the social impact and spiritual efficacy of the gift.
